generation.answer: The two sub-layers in each encoder layer of the Transformer are a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network [Attention Is All You Need, p. 3].
The base Transformer uses 8 parallel attention heads [Attention Is All You Need, p. 5].

The dot products are scaled by the square root of the key dimension (√dk) to counteract the effect of large dot products that can push the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients. This scaling helps maintain the stability of the gradients during training, especially for large values of dk [1, p. 4].

The Transformer injects information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence by adding "positional encodings" to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks. These positional encodings have the same dimension as the embeddings, allowing them to be summed. The authors use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies for the positional encodings, which are designed to help the model learn to attend by relative positions. They also experimented with learned positional embeddings and found that both versions produced nearly identical results, but chose the sinusoidal version for its potential to allow the model to extrapolate to longer sequence lengths than those encountered during training [Attention Is All You Need, p. 5].
The big Transformer achieved a BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task [Attention Is All You Need, p. 8].

Labelers preferred outputs from the 1.3B parameter InstructGPT model over outputs from the 175B GPT-3, despite the InstructGPT model having over 100x fewer parameters [Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback, p. 5].

The steps of the RLHF method used to train InstructGPT are: (1) supervised fine-tuning (SFT), (2) reward model (RM) training, and (3) reinforcement learning via proximal policy optimization (PPO) on this reward model [Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback, p. 3].

The PPO-ptx variant in InstructGPT is a model that incorporates updates on the pretraining mix during the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) process. This approach aims to reduce performance regressions on certain tasks while maintaining labeler preference scores. It is noted that the PPO-ptx model performs slightly worse at larger model sizes compared to other models, but it is still part of the InstructGPT framework that seeks to align language models with user instructions [Paper Title, p. 5].
GPT-4 passed a simulated version of the Uniform Bar Examination with a score in the top 10% of test takers [1, p. 1].

The GPT-4 report states that a large focus of the project was building a deep learning stack that scales predictably. This was important because extensive model-specific tuning is not feasible for very large training runs like GPT-4. To address this, the team developed infrastructure and optimization methods that exhibit predictable behavior across multiple scales. These improvements allowed for reliable predictions of some aspects of GPT-4's performance based on smaller models trained with significantly less compute, specifically between 1,000× to 10,000× less compute. The report also mentions that the final loss of properly-trained large language models is thought to be well approximated by power laws in the amount of compute used to train the model, and they successfully predicted GPT-4's final loss using this scaling law approach [GPT-4 Technical Report, p. 2].

The technical report describes several limitations of GPT-4, including:

1. It is not fully reliable and can "hallucinate" facts and make reasoning errors [1, p. 10].
2. GPT-4 lacks knowledge of events that occurred after its pre-training data cutoff in September 2021 [1, p. 10].
3. It can make simple reasoning errors and may be overly gullible in accepting false statements from users [1, p. 10].
4. The model can fail at hard problems, similar to human errors, such as introducing security vulnerabilities into code it produces [1, p. 10].
5. GPT-4 can be confidently wrong in its predictions and does not double-check its work when likely to make a mistake [1, p. 10].
6. Despite improvements, it still has similar limitations as earlier GPT models, such as a limited context window and not learning from experience [5, p. 1].

Mistral 7B uses grouped-query attention (GQA) and sliding window attention (SWA) to speed up inference. GQA significantly accelerates the inference speed and reduces memory requirements during decoding, while SWA effectively handles longer sequences at a reduced computational cost [2, p. 1].
The sliding window size in Mistral 7B is W = 4096 [Mistral 7B, p. 2].

Mistral 7B significantly outperforms Llama 2 13B across all evaluated benchmarks, including reasoning, mathematics, and code generation. It also approaches the coding performance of Code-Llama 7B without sacrificing performance on non-code benchmarks. In terms of instruction fine-tuning, Mistral 7B – Instruct surpasses Llama 2 13B – Chat model on both human and automated benchmarks [1, p. 4; 4, p. 1].
The Gemini family consists of three model sizes: Ultra, Pro, and Nano [Gemini: A Family of Highly Capable Multimodal Models, p. 4].

Gemini Ultra surpassed human-expert performance on the MMLU benchmark, scoring 90.0%, which has been a defacto measure of progress for LLMs since it was first released in 2020 [Gemini: A Family of Highly Capable Multimodal Models, p. 40].

3. The third paper mentions that GPT-4 has similar limitations as earlier models, including hallucinations, and discusses improvements in reducing hallucinations compared to previous versions [GPT-4 Technical Report, p. 10].

The second paper, "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback," details the process of fine-tuning language models using human feedback, including the collection of labeler demonstrations and rankings of model outputs to align the models with user intent [Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback, p. 1].
